articles.title: Meet Teddy Riner, the Decorated Olympian Running for French President
articles.summary: The French presidential election took an unexpected turn this week when Teddy Riner, a celebrated Olympian and judo star, announced his intention to run in the high-stakes race. “I know what people will say about me: ‘He’s mad. He isn’t part of the establishment. He doesn’t know the rules. articles.title: Biden Says He Would Have Stepped Down If He Knew He Had Cancer
articles.summary: Former President Joe Biden said in a recent interview that he wasn’t aware that he had cancer when he was in the White House—but that if he had known, he would have stepped down. articles.title: The Good Daughter Is One Exhausting Trauma Dump After Another
articles.summary: The Good Daughter opens with the kind of formative act of violence that thrillers typically save for climactic flashbacks. Two masked gunmen looking to exact revenge on a small-town Georgia defense lawyer invade his home to find only his wife and two daughters. This nightmare continues that day and reverberates through the girls’ adult lives. Front-loading this key trauma allows the Peacock series, premiering Nov. 12, to make it the basis of maybe a dozen more trauma dumps over the course of its six gloomy episodes

articles.title: Avedon Is a Gracefully Constructed Documentary About a Great American Photographer
articles.summary: Richard Avedon , whose career began in the early 1940s and ended with his death, following a cerebral hemorrhage, in 2004, was one of the greatest fashion photographers of his era. Even if you think you don’t care about fashion, you’ve probably been awed by his 1955 Dovima With Elephants, in which the supermodel Dovima, draped in a two-tone Dior gown, stands regally between two pachyderms, her arms outstretched as if to read their magnificence with her fingertips. articles.title: How to Check in on Your Friendships
articles.summary: You know your best friend’s coffee order, complicated family dynamics, and feelings about her boss. But you might not know whether she wishes you called more—or how much she appreciated that text you sent last week. “We have this expectation that friendships should be easy, that we should always be affirmed, that our friends are kind of there forever,” says Nick Fager, a therapist in New York.
